circulation_ratio.definition: `circulation_metrics.ratio` — dedicated circulation area over plan area
circulation_ratio.rationale: Circulation is overhead, but a house with none has no separation between public and private life; C26 already refuses the extreme (>0.24). Direction is deliberately `info`: lower is not simply better, which is precisely the trap §2A warns about.
circulation_ratio.limitations: Says nothing about the shape or usefulness of that circulation.

circulation_longest_segment_m.rationale: A long corridor is the clearest form of wasted movement; C26 refuses beyond 20 m.
circulation_longest_segment_m.limitations: A long corridor that serves many rooms is less wasteful than a short one that serves two.

circulation_dead_ends.definition: `circulation_metrics.dead_end_count` — corridor ends with neither a door nor an open join
circulation_dead_ends.rationale: A corridor end that serves nothing is pure waste and reads as a mistake.
circulation_dead_ends.limitations: Production's own threshold refuses only at 2+; one dead end is common.

circulation_turns.definition: `circulation_metrics.turn_count` — axis changes on the entrance-to-farthest-room path
circulation_turns.rationale: Turns make a route feel long and hard to read; production measures but never gates them.
circulation_turns.limitations: Counted on one representative path, not all routes.

circulation_duplicated_area_m2.definition: `circulation_metrics.duplicated_area_m2` — area of circulation rooms that redundantly serve an overlapping set of rooms
circulation_duplicated_area_m2.rationale: Two corridors doing one corridor's job.

circulation_rooms_served.definition: rooms reachable through one door directly off a HALL/CIRCULATION room
circulation_rooms_served.rationale: A corridor earns its area by distributing; the more rooms one circulation space serves directly, the less of the plan is spent on passage.

mean_steps_from_entrance.definition: mean doors crossed on the shortest realized-door path from the arrival room to every other room
mean_steps_from_entrance.rationale: How deep the plan is as actually walked.
mean_steps_from_entrance.limitations: Topological: one long corridor counts as one step.

max_steps_from_entrance.definition: worst-case door count from the arrival room to any room
max_steps_from_entrance.rationale: The room nobody wants to reach; catches a tacked-on wing.

mean_walk_from_entrance_m.definition: mean Manhattan distance from the entrance door centre to each room centroid
mean_walk_from_entrance_m.rationale: A metric rather than topological proxy for daily walking distance.
mean_walk_from_entrance_m.limitations: Manhattan through walls, not along the real route (see MISSING_INFORMATION).

dead_space_share.definition: `dead_space.dead_space_share` — STUB + SLIVER + CORNER + OVERSIZED_HALL area over plan area
dead_space_share.rationale: Production's own residual-pocket measure: area that is neither room nor useful passage.
dead_space_share.limitations: Its STUB limit is documented as stale and it gates nothing today.

public_private_wall_m.definition: total shared interior wall length between a PUBLIC_CORE room and a bedroom-class room
public_private_wall_m.rationale: Every metre of wall between the living core and a bedroom is noise and privacy transfer that circulation would otherwise absorb. Rubric section J records that NO production check measures whether delivered zoning stayed coherent — this is that gap.
public_private_wall_m.limitations: Wall length is not acoustics; a shared wall without a door is far milder than a door.

public_private_wall_share.definition: public_private_wall_m over the plan's total interior shared-wall length
public_private_wall_share.rationale: Normalises the raw length against plan size.

bedrooms_reached_through_public.definition: bedrooms with NO realized-door route from the arrival room that avoids every PUBLIC_CORE room other than the arrival room itself
bedrooms_reached_through_public.rationale: Reaching a bedroom across the living room is the classic zoning failure: residents cross the family's activity to go to bed and guests see the sleeping wing.
bedrooms_reached_through_public.limitations: Arriving INTO the living room is not counted here — that is entrance quality, measured by `arrival_is_circulation`, and would otherwise be charged twice.

public_components.definition: connected components of the PUBLIC_CORE rooms under shared-wall adjacency
public_components.rationale: A coherent public zone is one piece; two fragments means the living functions were scattered.
public_components.limitations: Rooms joined only through a hall count as separate here by design.

private_components.definition: connected components of the bedroom-class rooms plus their ensuites under shared-wall adjacency
private_components.inputs: room rects + roles + resolved wet rooms
private_components.rationale: A sleeping wing in one piece can be shut off from the rest of the house.
private_components.limitations: A two-wing house may legitimately split bedrooms.

zone_band_overlap.definition: overlap of the front-to-back (y) extents of the public cluster and the bedroom cluster, over the smaller extent
zone_band_overlap.rationale: Front-to-back stratification (public at the street, private at the back) is the band family's natural zoning move; heavy overlap means the zones are interleaved.
zone_band_overlap.limitations: Assumes a front/back reading; a left/right zoning scores badly without being wrong.

bedroom_doors_off_public.definition: bedroom-class rooms with a realized door into a PUBLIC_CORE room
bedroom_doors_off_public.rationale: A bedroom door onto the living room exposes the room every time it is used.
bedroom_doors_off_public.limitations: Door existence, not its position on the wall or any screening.

bedroom_doors_off_arrival.definition: bedroom-class rooms with a realized door into the room the front door arrives in
bedroom_doors_off_arrival.rationale: The most exposed case: the bedroom is on show at the front door.
bedroom_doors_off_arrival.limitations: Treats the arrival room as one undivided space.

master_hall_sight_line_to_bed.definition: `master_suite.hall_sight_line_to_bed` — a straight ray from the master's entry door reaches the conservative bed envelope
master_hall_sight_line_to_bed.rationale: The only room-level sight-line computation in the repository besides the wet rooms'. Being visible in bed from the corridor is a real privacy defect.
master_hall_sight_line_to_bed.limitations: Master bedroom only; the bed envelope is a conservative placeholder, not a furniture layout. No equivalent exists for secondary bedrooms (see MISSING_INFORMATION).

master_suite_score.definition: `master_suite.suite_score` — weighted sum of: ensuite route crosses the bed (1.0), wardrobe route crosses the bed (0.5), hall sight line to bed (0.3), hall sight line to ensuite door (0.2)
master_suite_score.rationale: Production's own master-suite privacy measure, computed today and wired to nothing.
master_suite_score.limitations: Its weights are production's, not derived here; master only.

wet_doors_to_public.rationale: A bathroom opening off a public room is the complaint specs/009 and C29 were written about.
wet_doors_to_public.limitations: Uses production's classification, including its decision that LIVING access is legal.

wet_direct_sight_lines.rationale: A bathroom door facing straight into a public room.

wet_privacy_worst.definition: worst `WetPrivacy.privacy_score` in the plan (production's own exposure + obstruction - adjacency combination, already used as a ranking key in `_break_l_tie`)
wet_privacy_worst.rationale: Production's existing privacy ranking key, applied to every plan rather than only L peers.
wet_privacy_worst.limitations: Wet rooms only; production's own scale.

entrance_to_bedroom_steps.definition: fewest doors from the arrival room to any bedroom-class room
entrance_to_bedroom_steps.rationale: Separation of the sleeping zone from the front door. Reported, never ranked: more separation is more private but less convenient, and that trade-off is a taste the brief does not state.

arrival_is_circulation.definition: `entrance_sequence.is_circulation_arrival` — the front door arrives into HALL/CIRCULATION
arrival_is_circulation.rationale: A transition space lets a visitor be received without entering the family's living space; `ENTRANCE_ZONE_PRIORITY` ranks hall, then circulation, then living, and `general_pipeline`'s own `_entrance_rank` already prefers it.
arrival_is_circulation.limitations: Arriving into a generous living room is a legitimate open-plan choice — specs/009 decision C ranks it third, not forbidden.

entrance_pocket_m.definition: `entrance_sequence.pocket_length_m` — dead length of the arrival space beyond the first opening (C25 refuses beyond 4.0 m)
entrance_pocket_m.rationale: An arrival that runs into a blank pocket is the anti-pattern 'entrance dead-end'.

entrance_distance_to_public_m.definition: `entrance_sequence.distance_to_public_m` — distance from the front door to the first public room
entrance_distance_to_public_m.rationale: Excessive travel immediately after entry (§2D); production's own `entrance_sequence_prefers` ranks on exactly this and IS wired into `general_pipeline`.
entrance_distance_to_public_m.limitations: Distance only; says nothing about what is passed on the way.

entrance_private_doors_passed.definition: `entrance_sequence.private_doors_passed` — private-room doors passed on the way to the public zone
entrance_private_doors_passed.rationale: Walking past bedroom doors to reach the living room is both a privacy and an arrival defect.
entrance_private_doors_passed.limitations: Counted on the measured route only.

arrival_fanout.definition: realized doors in the arrival room, excluding the front door
arrival_fanout.rationale: An entrance should distribute; a fanout of 1 makes the arrival a corridor stub.
arrival_fanout.limitations: High fanout can also mean every door is visible from the front door — read with `bedroom_doors_off_arrival`.

steps_entrance_to_living.definition: doors crossed from the arrival room to LIVING (0 when arrival IS the living room)
steps_entrance_to_living.rationale: The main public destination should be immediately available.

public_zone_coherent.definition: `public_composition.public_zone_coherent` — the public rooms form one coherent related group
public_zone_coherent.rationale: Production's own public-composition measure (Issue #41), already ranked on by `composition_prefers` in `general_pipeline`.
public_zone_coherent.limitations: Production's own definition of 'related', which includes open joins and doors.

kitchen_dining_related.definition: `public_composition.kitchen_dining_related` (1/0; absent pair reported as 1 — not a defect)
kitchen_dining_related.rationale: Serving between kitchen and dining is daily use; KITCHEN-LIVING is also the highest-lift measured adjacency in the ResPlan corpus.
kitchen_dining_related.limitations: `None` when the brief has no separate dining room, which is not a defect.

living_exterior_exposed.rationale: The main living space should reach the facade.

public_largest_cluster_share.definition: net area of the largest shared-wall-connected public cluster over the total public net area
public_largest_cluster_share.rationale: How much of the public programme actually hangs together as one space.
public_largest_cluster_share.limitations: A deliberately separated formal dining room reads as fragmentation.

public_narrowest_neck_m.definition: smallest shared wall between two adjacent rooms inside the largest public cluster
public_narrowest_neck_m.rationale: A public zone joined by a 0.9 m neck is two rooms, not one space (§2E 'narrow necks').
public_narrowest_neck_m.limitations: Falls back to the cluster's own width for a single-room cluster.

public_compactness.definition: net area of the largest public cluster over its bounding-box area
public_compactness.rationale: A compact public zone is a usable space; an L of leftovers is not.

public_worst_aspect.definition: largest net long/short ratio among the PUBLIC_CORE rooms
public_worst_aspect.rationale: A 4:1 living room cannot be furnished as one space; the rubric records KITCHEN median aspect 2.75 and DINING 2.35 against real plans as a known strip-room gap.
public_worst_aspect.limitations: Per room; says nothing about the combined shape.

bedroom_worst_aspect.definition: `hub_guard.PlanProportions.bedroom_max` — worst secondary-bedroom aspect (production's own gate value, HUB_GATES.bedroom_aspect = 1.35)
bedroom_worst_aspect.rationale: A narrow bedroom cannot take a bed with circulation on both sides; the quality tier's `preferred_aspect_ratio` for a bedroom is 1.5 against a legal max of 2.5.
bedroom_worst_aspect.limitations: Gross rect, as production computes it.

master_aspect.rationale: Same, for the one bedroom the programme singles out.

bedroom_min_net_area_m2.definition: smallest net area among bedroom-class rooms
bedroom_min_net_area_m2.rationale: The worst bedroom is what a family argues about.
bedroom_min_net_area_m2.limitations: Area alone; a large awkward room still scores well here.

bedroom_min_short_side_m.definition: smallest net short side among bedroom-class rooms
bedroom_min_short_side_m.rationale: Usable width governs whether furniture fits at all.
bedroom_min_short_side_m.limitations: The furniture feasibility flag is reported separately.

bedroom_area_cv.definition: coefficient of variation of net area across the SECONDARY bedrooms (BEDROOM role only)
bedroom_area_cv.rationale: Secondary bedrooms are normally meant to be comparable; one child getting half the room of another is a complaint, not a design.
bedroom_area_cv.limitations: Assumes secondary bedrooms SHOULD be comparable — a documented assumption, false if a brief distinguishes them, which these briefs do not.

master_is_largest_bedroom.definition: 1 when MASTER_BEDROOM has the largest net area among bedroom-class rooms
master_is_largest_bedroom.rationale: The one bedroom hierarchy the programme states by naming the role.

bedrooms_with_window.definition: fraction of bedroom-class rooms with at least one placeable window
bedrooms_with_window.rationale: Daylight is REQUIRED for bedrooms and gated by C19/C8; the fraction exposes plans that satisfy it minimally.
bedrooms_with_window.limitations: Window count, not area or orientation.

bedroom_public_wall_m.definition: total shared wall between bedroom-class and PUBLIC_CORE rooms
bedroom_public_wall_m.rationale: Noise at the pillow; the per-bedroom view of the zoning metric.

bedrooms_entered_from_circulation.definition: fraction of bedroom-class rooms whose realized door comes from HALL/CIRCULATION
bedrooms_entered_from_circulation.rationale: The access policy's own preference for private rooms, measured on the built result.
bedrooms_entered_from_circulation.limitations: Legality is already hard-gated; this measures how uniformly it was achieved.

plumbing_complexity_index.definition: `wet_core.plumbing_complexity_index` — estimated independent plumbing stacks (components over wet rooms plus the kitchen)
plumbing_complexity_index.rationale: Fewer stacks is real build cost; production's own estimate, with a ranking key (`candidate_wet_core_key`) that has no caller.
plumbing_complexity_index.limitations: An ESTIMATE by its own docstring; no riser or slab routing.

wet_shared_wall_m.definition: `wet_core.shared_wall_length_m` — interior wall shared between two wet rooms
wet_shared_wall_m.rationale: Back-to-back wet rooms share one wet wall.
wet_shared_wall_m.limitations: Clustering can also bury a bathroom; balanced by `wet_rooms_with_window`.

wet_cluster_count.limitations: An ensuite legitimately sits away from a guest WC; a preference, not a rule.

wet_adjacency_share.definition: `hub_guard.PlanProportions.wet_share` — wet rooms adjacent to their served room over all wet rooms (production's own gate value, HUB_GATES.wet_adjacency = 0.80)
wet_adjacency_share.rationale: The rubric records this as the single largest measured quality gap after circulation topology: 40% against a ~85-90% reference.

wet_rooms_with_window.definition: fraction of wet rooms with at least one placeable window
wet_rooms_with_window.rationale: Guards the clustering metrics: a tight wet core that lands every bathroom in the dark is not better. Bathrooms are PREFERRED (not REQUIRED) exposure, so this never gates.

ensuite_adjacent_to_host.definition: fraction of resolved ENSUITE wet rooms sharing a wall with their declared host bedroom
ensuite_adjacent_to_host.rationale: An ensuite must belong to its bedroom; the door proves access, the wall proves it is part of the suite rather than reached around a corner.
ensuite_adjacent_to_host.limitations: 1.0 when the brief has no ensuite.

preferred_exposure_satisfied.definition: fraction of rooms whose exposure policy is PREFERRED that have an exterior wall
preferred_exposure_satisfied.rationale: The exposure the policy wants but never enforces — the honest place to reward daylight beyond the validators.
preferred_exposure_satisfied.limitations: Exterior wall, not window area or orientation.

two_sided_exposure_share.definition: `l_massing_guard.ExposureProportions.two_sided_share` — habitable rooms with two or more exterior sides
two_sided_exposure_share.rationale: Dual-aspect rooms get cross light and ventilation; production already ranks L-massing on it.
two_sided_exposure_share.limitations: Counts sides, not their orientation or view.

windowless_rooms.definition: rooms with no placeable window whose exposure policy is REQUIRED or PREFERRED
windowless_rooms.rationale: A room the policy wants daylit and did not get.
windowless_rooms.limitations: REQUIRED misses are already impossible in a PASS plan, so this counts PREFERRED misses.

max_single_room_facade_share.definition: longest exterior wall run belonging to one room over the footprint perimeter
max_single_room_facade_share.rationale: One room monopolising the facade starves the rest (§2H).
max_single_room_facade_share.limitations: Perimeter share, not the solar value of each side.

public_facade_share.definition: exterior wall length of PUBLIC_CORE rooms over the footprint perimeter
public_facade_share.rationale: The rooms people spend the day in should get the frontage.
public_facade_share.limitations: Treats every side as equal (see MISSING_INFORMATION on orientation).

bedroom_facade_share.definition: exterior wall length of bedroom-class rooms over the footprint perimeter
bedroom_facade_share.rationale: Bedrooms need their own frontage for light and air.

street_facade_public_share.definition: fraction of the street-edge facade held by PUBLIC_CORE rooms
street_facade_public_share.rationale: Who faces the street is an architectural stance (public front versus private front), not a quality: reported, never ranked.
street_facade_public_share.limitations: Street side taken from the footprint only.

mean_net_aspect.definition: mean net long/short ratio over all rooms
mean_net_aspect.rationale: The plan's overall tendency to squeeze rooms.
mean_net_aspect.limitations: A mean hides one terrible room.

max_net_aspect.definition: largest net long/short ratio over all rooms
max_net_aspect.rationale: The worst-shaped room, which is what a reader notices first.
max_net_aspect.limitations: Every room is already inside its own template bound, so differences here are quality, not legality.

worst_wet_aspect.rationale: Wet rooms are where strip shapes concentrate; production already ranks L-massing on it.

sliver_rooms.definition: inhabited rooms (not wet, service or circulation) with a net short side below 2.0 m
sliver_rooms.rationale: Below roughly two metres a habitable room stops being usable whatever its area.
sliver_rooms.limitations: The 2.0 m line is a documented judgement; production's own sliver floor (0.9 m) only catches leftovers.

min_net_short_side_m.definition: smallest net short side over all rooms
min_net_short_side_m.rationale: The tightest dimension anywhere in the plan.
min_net_short_side_m.limitations: Wet and service rooms legitimately set this.

furniture_fit_share.definition: fraction of rooms whose furniture envelope fits (production's C9 feasibility record)
furniture_fit_share.rationale: The only furniture signal the pipeline produces today.
furniture_fit_share.limitations: A boolean per room: fits or not. Real layout quality (usable wall lengths, clearances) is measured by `furnishability.py`, whose C30 is defined but NOT called by `validate` — see MISSING_INFORMATION.

soft_adjacency_lift.definition: mean ResPlan corpus adjacency LIFT over realized touching pairs whose BOTH roles the corpus can measure (LIVING, KITCHEN, BEDROOM, BATHROOM, BALCONY only)
soft_adjacency_lift.rationale: The only non-invented source of soft adjacency preference in the repository: how often real architects put these two roles together relative to chance.
soft_adjacency_lift.limitations: Covers 5 roles; HALL, DINING, MASTER_BEDROOM, SAFE_ROOM, TOILET and the rest are explicitly UNMEASURABLE by that corpus. Frequency in real plans is also not desirability — and the corpus is apartments, where for example BEDROOM-LIVING touching is near-universal (lift 1.89) in a way a detached house need not copy.

measurable_adjacency_coverage.definition: fraction of realized touching pairs for which the prior had data
measurable_adjacency_coverage.rationale: States how much of the plan the adjacency prior could see at all — the honesty term for the metric above.
measurable_adjacency_coverage.limitations: Low coverage means the lift is weak evidence, not that the plan is bad.
